text:
Ibrahim: thanks for the runtime roadmap talk today. dropping a compact thread for a few follow-ups on dynamic batching, prefix cache durability, and kernel sequencing. please reply with clarifications or actions. :wave:

Sofia: quick Q 1 for dynamic batching heuristics  do we use length-based sharding or just time-window grouping? tiny chat messages got slower in the pilot.

Marta: good call. current approach is hybrid: primary sharding by estimated token-length bracket, then time-window (default 8ms) to fill batches. short-chat routes are auto-placed in the "low-latency" bracket which keeps batch size=1.

Liam: can teams tweak the brackets per-model? e.g., put our conversational route in more aggressive binning?

Marta: yes, model-profile supports `\{"length_buckets": [32,128,512], "latency_priority": true}`. Console will expose simple toggles for Dedicated customers.

Sofia: prefix/KV cache persistence  any update on cross-host warm-up? we saw reschedules where hot prefixes were cold for minutes.

Ibrahim: design update: Dedicated will get async snapshot + oplog replication to a shared store (configurable). Hosted remains per-host with aggressive prefetch for hot prefixes. reschedules will trigger proactive prefetch for recently-used prefixes (N minutes window).

Liam: risk to latency SLOs during oplog syncs?

Ibrahim: syncs are background and rate-limited. worst-case the system falls back to fast-path RPCs; expect small p99 blips during large rebalances. ops will surface route-level alerts if blips > threshold.

Marta: kernel prioritization question: is fused-attn the top lift this cycle? customers ask about int8 speedups too.

Ibrahim: fused-attn gets the major allocation for long-context models (big p50/p95 wins). int8 GEMM and bf16 kernels are in parallel but on a smaller stream. we're coordinating releases so customers see staged improvements per-hardware family.

Sofia: can Dedicated customers opt into experimental kernels? we'd like to test on our reserved pool before host rollout.

Ibrahim: yes  model-profile flag "kernel_profile": "experimental" allows opt-in. rollout plan: opt-in -> small canary (staging) -> customer opt-in on Dedicated -> promote to Hosted. fallback path auto-switches to safe kernel on errors.

Liam: what are the regression gates for quantized kernels? acceptance criteria?

Marta: gates are: unit-op tests, model-level eval on our 1k-prompt suite with allowed quality delta <= 1.5% on the primary metric, and stress stability runs (48h) for memory leaks.

Sofia: who owns the eval set updates? i'll volunteer to help add conversational prompts.

Marta: thanks  ML infra + Marta own the harness; @Sofia please DM me and i'll add you to the eval PRs.

ci-bot: task created -> "add conversational prompts to eval harness" assigned to Sofia, due 1783460000.

Ibrahim: ops note: we're adding a SKU-compatibility matrix that lists memory delta for kernel+cache combos per GPU SKU and recommended batch caps. will publish as a one-pager for Product/Docs.

deploy-bot: canary started: "fused-attn-alpha" ts=1783456900 target=3% staging monitors=[latency,p99-errors,oom].

Liam: thanks all. please drop canary results and the one-pager link here. closing the loop for now. :thumbsup:
